clinician.trajectory_summary: Male infant born at 38 weeks 4 days (birth weight 2.45 kg) with prenatal-onset multisystem disease caused by a de novo heterozygous COL4A1 c.2771G>A variant. Prenatal imaging (ultrasound, fetal MRI, fetal echocardiography) documented CNS anomalies including microcephaly, polymicrogyria, multifocal hemorrhagic/ischemic infarcts, ex-vacuo dilatation, corpus callosum dysgenesis, optic nerve hypoplasia, and vermian hypoplasia, along with cardiac defects (dilated right chamber, hypoplastic left chambers, moderate muscular VSD, and narrow aortic arch). At birth, the infant presented with signs of poor perfusion (dusky feet, cool extremities, limp) and respiratory failure requiring positive pressure ventilation and CPAP. Postnatal echocardiography confirmed fenestrated atrial septum, moderate mid-muscular VSD, hypoplastic left ventricle and aortic arch, PDA, and suprasystemic RV systolic pressure. EEG documented frequent subclinical seizures. Postnatal brain MRI confirmed the prenatal CNS findings. The infant was managed with cardiac support (diuretics for VSD pulmonary over-circulation: hydrochlorothiazide-spironolactone) and seizure management (phenobarbital, levetiracetam, lacosamide). Clinical course showed progressive improvement with successful weaning to room air and transition to oral feeds. The infant was discharged on room air with continued diuretic and antiepileptic medications under Neurology follow-up.

final.trajectory_summary: Male infant born at 38 weeks 4 days (birth weight 2.45 kg) with prenatal-onset multisystem disease caused by a de novo heterozygous COL4A1 c.2771G>A variant. Prenatal imaging (ultrasound, fetal MRI, fetal echocardiography) documented CNS anomalies including microcephaly, polymicrogyria, multifocal hemorrhagic/ischemic infarcts, ex-vacuo dilatation, corpus callosum dysgenesis, optic nerve hypoplasia, and vermian hypoplasia, along with cardiac defects (dilated right chamber, hypoplastic left chambers, moderate muscular VSD, and narrow aortic arch). At birth, the infant presented with signs of poor perfusion (dusky feet, cool extremities, limp) and respiratory failure requiring positive pressure ventilation and CPAP. Postnatal echocardiography confirmed fenestrated atrial septum, moderate mid-muscular VSD, hypoplastic left ventricle and aortic arch, PDA, and suprasystemic RV systolic pressure. EEG documented frequent subclinical seizures. Postnatal brain MRI confirmed the prenatal CNS findings. The infant was managed with cardiac support (diuretics for VSD pulmonary over-circulation: hydrochlorothiazide-spironolactone) and seizure management (phenobarbital, levetiracetam, lacosamide). Clinical course showed progressive improvement with successful weaning to room air and transition to oral feeds. The infant was discharged on room air with continued diuretic and antiepileptic medications under Neurology follow-up.
